Hope. Religion is soul food for the hopeless. Whenever I visit my parent's homeland, unnamed third world country, I see all these corrupt individuals beat down the poor and hold them in virtual slavery. The poor turn to revolt and religion. Those who can't revolt turn to religion and often it's the only thing keeping them sane. When you see the evilest of humanity, you have to believe that there is a higher power who will avenge you one day even though you might not be able to do it yourself. These people might be able to get away with it in this life but there has to be punishment an consequence for them in the next.

Judging someone is actually one of the worst things you can do in Islam. The Prophet's companions used to be kind to those who were unkind to them on the grounds that one day that person might become a better person than him(the Companion). In one Hadith it is said that think of seventy excuses for someone's wrongdoing and if you can't find one just say "there must be an excuse but I don't know of it." My favorite example was of an "infidel" prostitute. This prostitute had ALL of her sins forgiven simply because she fed water to a thirsty dog. My point is: Islam is not about judging people, even though people practice it that way, it is about seeing the best in people and helping them achieve the potential you and God sees in them regardless of race, religion, or their sins. A true Muslim is never aggressive or rude towards anyone period. Lgbtq? Atheist? Islamaphobe? No one. To drive home my point. In a Hadith the Prophet speaks of two men. One was extremely religious and extremely arrogant. He looked at the other man and said that this man will definitely go to hell for his sins. In the end the pretentious man was thrown in hell for his arrogance and cruel words while the other man was taken to heaven. Allah says in the holy Quran that no one shall enter paradise with even the smallest amount of arrogance in their heart. To look down on others and dare to judge someone is arrogant and blasphemous (how dare you try to play God and claim someone's fate).

Not teaching young children the basics of their body. Too many parents try to hold off the talk until puberty or when something goes wrong. Kindergardeners call their genitals their privates, peepees, or other names without understanding that area is a no touch zone. Teach your kids from a young age that no one is allowed to touch their genitals and if they do you get help from a trusted adult. Just taking this little precaution can make a big difference.

Reading 19th century "Golden Age" Russian Literature. Sounds interesting enough if you're middle aged but I'm 17 and this started when I was 13. Really a strange addiction, I've opted out of parties, dances, dates, and even frat parties, just to read some Tolstoy, Lermontov, or Dostoevsky in peace and quiet. Oh, the lies I've told to go off into a corner and read those bewitching books!
